stories.title: Add the pose limits and a function that clamps a pose to them
stories.description: Create src/carm/limits.ts with the allowed range of each pose value (F3.1): oblique −90…+90° (negative = left, positive = right, ±90° = lateral), tilt −40° (caudal) … +40° (cranial), table left/right ±200 mm, head/foot ±400 mm, height ±150 mm. Add clampPose(pose), which returns a pose with every value inside its range (a value that is not a finite number becomes 0), and a small function every later control uses to change the pose in the store through clampPose (e.g. changePose(store, patch)). Plain TypeScript, no browser code, no edits in src/core/.
acceptance: Unit test: values inside the ranges are returned unchanged
Unit test: each of the five values is clamped at both ends (e.g. oblique 120 → 90, tilt −55 → −40, table left/right 500 → 200, head/foot −900 → −400, height 151 → 150)
Unit test: NaN and Infinity become 0
Unit test: changing the pose through the store function stores the clamped pose and a new pose object (so store subscribers are told)

stories.title: Add a slider with a number readout for each of the five pose values
stories.description: In the C-arm panel add five sliders (<input type="range">, step 1, ranges from limits.ts) with a label and a number readout each. Test ids: slider-oblique, slider-tilt, slider-table-left-right, slider-table-head-foot, slider-table-height, and readout-oblique … readout-table-height. Readouts show the signed number with its unit ('25°', '-10°', '15 mm'); the slider ends are labelled with their meaning (L / R, CAUD / CRAN, and so on). Moving a slider changes the pose in the store through the clamping function from F3-S1; the sliders and readouts also follow the store when the pose changes elsewhere. Moving a slider must NOT take an image. Add the zone's screen-test helper tests/e2e/carm/controls.ts (not a spec file) with a function that drags a slider handle: mouse drag in the desktop set-up, touch drag in the tablet set-up (Playwright has no built-in touch drag; a CDP session with Input.dispatchTouchEvent touchStart / touchMove / touchEnd works in Chromium). Layout: the C-arm panel is one quarter of the screen (F0 layout; about 500×370 px in the tablet set-up) and will hold five sliders, the Shot and Fluoro buttons, two counters, the region picker and a help button — keep rows compact and put small items side by side. Every button and every slider's touch area (the box of its <input> element) is at least 44 px wide and 44 px tall, and this zone's own screen tests check it (F12 cannot fix another zone's panel); F12 owns the final layout.
acceptance: Screen test (desktop: mouse drag; tablet: touch drag): dragging each of the five slider handles changes that value in window.__sim.getState().pose, and the readout shows the same number
Screen test (both set-ups): dragging a slider all the way to an end gives exactly the limit from F3.1
Screen test (both set-ups): changing the pose in the store (setPose from tests/fixtures/simPage.ts) moves the slider and its readout to the new value
Screen test (both set-ups): dragging a slider leaves the shot count unchanged
Screen test (both set-ups): all five sliders and the Shot button are visible without scrolling the page
Screen test (both set-ups): the oblique slider's ends are labelled 'L' and 'R', the tilt slider's 'CAUD' and 'CRAN', and each table slider has a visible label at both ends
Screen test (both set-ups): each of the five sliders' touch area (the box of its <input> element) is at least 44 px wide and 44 px tall

stories.title: Add keyboard shortcuts that step each pose value
stories.description: Add keyboard shortcuts for the pose. Keep the key list in one file (src/carm/keymap.ts) so it is easy to change and so the help overlay (next story) can list it. Planning choice, the owner may change it (the spec does not name the keys; these avoid the keys reserved for the needle in F5 — W, S, Q, E, arrow keys — and Space and F): J / L = oblique left / right, I / K = tilt cranial / caudal, N / M = table toward the patient's right / left, U / O = table toward the head / feet, Y / H = table up / down. Match keys by their position (event.code), so other keyboard layouts work. Each press steps an angle by 1°, or by 5° with Shift held; table moves are always 5 mm. Results are clamped to the limits. Put the stepping in a plain function (pose, key, shift → new pose) for unit tests. Shortcuts follow the existing spacebar rules in src/carm/index.ts: ignored while the disclaimer is shown and while typing in a text field.
acceptance: Unit test: each of the ten keys changes only its own value, in the documented direction, by 1° (angles) or 5 mm (table)
Unit test: with Shift an angle key steps 5°; a table key still steps 5 mm
Unit test: stepping past a limit stays at the limit

Screen test (desktop only; the tablet set-up has no keyboard and uses the sliders from F3-S2): pressing L three times and Shift+I once gives oblique +3 and tilt +5 in window.__sim.getState().pose, the readouts show the same, and the shot count is unchanged
Screen test (desktop only): the keys do nothing while the disclaimer is shown
stories.verify: npx vitest run tests/carm/keymap.test.ts && npx playwright test tests/e2e/carm/shortcuts.spec.ts

stories.title: Add the continuous-fluoro logic (frames and time counting) as plain functions
stories.description: Create src/carm/fluoro.ts, plain TypeScript with the clock passed in (no browser code), so it is unit-testable: start(now), frame(now) and stop(now). While running, each frame records the current pose as the last image pose, sets the store's lastImageKind to 'fluoro' (shared contract, 2026-11-10; a single shot sets 'shot') and emits one 'exposure' event (the renderer redraws on it); frames never change the shot count. The fluoro time in the store grows during the hold: each frame adds the real time since the previous frame (or since start), and stop adds the rest, so the total is the real time between start and stop, measured from the clock values — not by counting frames — and slow frames do not lose time. Starting twice or stopping when not running does nothing. A single shot (takeShot) keeps working as before.
acceptance: Unit test: start at t = 0, frames at 100 ms steps, stop at t = 2000 ms adds 2.0 s (within 0.05 s) to the fluoro time, whatever the number of frames
Unit test: every frame while running emits exactly one 'exposure' event and sets the last image pose to the pose at that moment; the shot count never changes
Unit test: a frame call when not running emits nothing; after stop, frames emit nothing
Unit test: a second start while running, or a stop when not running, changes nothing
Unit test: two separate holds add up (1.0 s + 0.5 s = 1.5 s)
Unit test: after a start at t = 0 and one frame at t = 500 ms the fluoro time is already 0.5 s (within 0.05 s), before any stop
Unit test: each frame sets lastImageKind to 'fluoro'; a single shot afterwards sets it back to 'shot'

stories.title: Run continuous fluoro while the F key is held (desktop)
stories.description: Wire the fluoro logic to the keyboard: fluoro runs while the F key is held (key repeats ignored). While running, draw one frame per animation frame (requestAnimationFrame) and show the growing fluoro time; window.__sim.carm().fluoroOn is true. Take the start and stop times from the key events' own time stamps (event.timeStamp), not from when the handler happens to run, because frames are slow on the test machine's software GPU. Stop on key-up, when the window loses focus and when the page is hidden — fluoro must never keep running by itself. Screen tests move the C-arm with a pose key. The timing test holds F for about 3 seconds and compares the added fluoro time with the time between the keydown and keyup events as seen in the page (the test adds its own listeners that record event.timeStamp), not with the test's own stopwatch. The tablet set-up has no keyboard; the on-screen pedal and the tablet tests are the next story (F3-S11). Shortcuts follow the existing spacebar rules in src/carm/index.ts: ignored while the disclaimer is shown and while typing in a text field.
acceptance: Screen test (desktop): while F is held, changing the pose changes the canvas pixels (read with tests/fixtures/readCanvas.ts at the projected vertebra block centres and other fixed points) without any Shot; the shot count stays the same
Screen test (desktop): after releasing F, changing the pose again leaves those canvas pixels unchanged

Screen test (desktop): holding F for about 3 seconds adds the time between the keydown and keyup events (as recorded in the page) to window.__sim.carm().fluoroTimeSeconds within 10%, and the fluoro-time counter shows the same value to one decimal
Screen test (desktop): while F is held, a window 'blur' event stops fluoro: fluoroOn becomes false and the fluoro time stops growing
Screen test (desktop): F does nothing while the disclaimer is shown

stories.title: Check last image hold: moving the C-arm without taking an image leaves the picture unchanged
stories.description: Add the screen test for F3.5. Take an image, record a fingerprint of the canvas (grey values at a fixed grid of points, read with tests/fixtures/readCanvas.ts), move the C-arm with the sliders (and, on desktop, with a pose key), and check the fingerprint is unchanged while window.__sim.getState().pose has changed and lastImagePose has not. Then take a new image and check the fingerprint does change. The behaviour should already hold. If it does not, do not fix it here: the held image belongs to the render zone, so mark this story blocked and explain what you saw.
acceptance: Screen test (both set-ups): after moving oblique and tilt with the sliders, the canvas fingerprint equals the one before the move, pose differs from lastImagePose, and the shot count is unchanged
Screen test (both set-ups): one more Shot (spacebar on desktop, tap on tablet) raises the shot count by exactly 1, sets lastImagePose to the new pose and changes the fingerprint

stories.title: Let the region picker list the regions on offer and ask for the one the learner picks
stories.description: Use the shared contract added on 2026-11-10 (src/core/, read-only here): store.regions holds the regions on offer as { name, title } entries (filled by the anatomy zone, F1), and the bus event 'regionRequest' carries a region name. The picker lists store.regions (plus the loaded region if it is not among them, e.g. 'Phantom') and follows the store when the list or the loaded volume changes. When the learner picks an entry other than the loaded region, emit exactly one 'regionRequest' with its name; the picker itself loads nothing and keeps showing the region that is actually loaded (the store's volume) until a new volume arrives. Picking a region does not take an image and does not change the counters. F1's loader may not be merged yet, so the tests fill store.regions, listen on the bus and put a new volume in the store themselves, through the dev server's store module. No edits in src/core/ or src/anatomy/. This is the feature's last loop story: run the whole check.
acceptance: Unit test: for regions cervical and lumbosacral with 'phantom' loaded, the entries are those two followed by Phantom; with 'lumbosacral' loaded there are exactly the two
Screen test (both set-ups): after the test puts two regions in store.regions, the picker shows one option per region plus 'Phantom', and 'Phantom' is still selected
Screen test (both set-ups): choosing a region emits exactly one 'regionRequest' with its name; the shot count and the canvas are unchanged
Screen test (both set-ups): when the test then puts a volume with that region name in the store, the picker shows that region as selected
Screen test (both set-ups): the picker's touch area is at least 44 px tall
npm run check passes

stories.notes: Unblocked at the 2026-11-10 story review: the shared contract now has store.regions and the bus event 'regionRequest' (src/core/store.ts). Owner answers 2026-11-12 (docs/DECISIONS.md): 'Phantom' is not kept once real regions exist — it is listed only while it is the loaded volume (exactly the 'plus the loaded region if it is not among them' rule; no change to the acceptance criteria); the lumbar region (lumbosacral) loads at start, which is F1/F12 work, not this story. The end-to-end check with F1's loader is F1-S27.
